sentences.text: Lambeosaurus is the namesake of the subfamily Lambeosaurinae and the tribe Lambeosaurini, a group of hadrosaurids distinguished mainly by their elaborate skulls.
The skull of this dinosaur is distinctively characterized by an elaborate, narrow, and tall crest that rises above the head.
It possessed a neck with 14 or 15 cervical vertebrae, a count intermediate between Olorotitan and Parasaurolophus.
Scale impressions have been preserved in three Lambeosaurus specimens, providing rare details about its skin.
Species such as L. lambei, L. magnicristatus, and L. clavinitialis grew to approximately 7 to 7.7 meters in length and weighed between 2.6 and 3.4 tonnes.
There are 19 recorded fossil occurrences of Lambeosaurus known to science.
The genus Lambeosaurus was named by William A. Parks in 1923.
Lawrence M. Lambe led three expeditions in 1897, 1898, and 1901 to find fossils in Alberta.
American Museum of Natural History excavations in the Red Deer River region were conducted primarily by Brown between 1909 and 1914.
A species named L. laticaudus in 1981 was later reclassified into the separate genus Magnapaulia.
Lambeosaurus possessed extensive dental batteries, a unique feeding apparatus also found in ceratopsids.
Microscopic tooth wear indicates Lambeosaurus used a combination of propalinal and pleurokinetic motions for chewing, involving an oblique up-down stroke and front-back grinding.
During growth, the Lambeosaurus snout became slightly longer while the maxilla, skull height excluding the crest, and brain size decreased proportionally.
The environment featured a wet ground with a canopy of conifers and an understory of ferns, tree ferns, and flowering plants.
Rivers were lined with dense vegetation, and periodic flooding created swamps and mires that formed coal deposits.
The large theropods coexisting with Lambeosaurus were Gorgosaurus and an unnamed species of Daspletosaurus.
Other phylogenetic studies have found Lambeosaurus to be either the most basal lambeosaurine closely related to Corythosaurus, or an intermediate member within Lambeosaurini.
Parks named the genus Lambeosaurus and established the subfamily Lambeosaurinae to replace Stephanosaurinae because no crested skull was known for Stephanosaurus.
William Diller Matthew considered the name Procheneosaurus a nomen nudum, an informal name not valid for taxonomy, in 1921.
Lambeosaurus lived during the Late Cretaceous period in western North America.

Lambeosaurus lived during the late Cretaceous period, approximately 76 to 75 million years ago in the Campanian stage, though other estimates suggest a broader range from 83.6 to 72.2 million years ago, or a more specific span of 76.47 to 74.44 million years ago.
Lambeosaurus fossils are found between 17 and 52 meters above the contact, spanning the upper portions of MAZ-1 and MAZ-2.
Hypotheses for the crest's function have included underwater feeding, improved smell, thermoregulation, sodium regulation, communication, or sexual identification.
In 1962, Ostrom proposed that the crest evolved to redirect the olfactory bulb upwards to increase the sense of smell.
